title: Podium - Small Business Tools: Has its ups and downs - Small blue collar businesses read
text: Podium has definitely had its ups and downs for our small landscaping business. There are positives to the platform, and it has helped organize communication and reviews better than normal texting in some ways, but we’ve also noticed several areas where it significantly lacks. One of the biggest issues is reliability in areas with poor cellular reception. When working out in the field, it can become almost impossible to send texts or images. If a message fails to send, there also seems to be a bug where the app continuously shows the message trying to send indefinitely, especially with photos attached. We’ve also run into frustrations with character limits causing longer client messages to split into multiple texts, which wasn’t an issue when using standard iPhone messaging. Phone calls through the app can also be difficult depending on jobsite location and service quality. There are additional features we wish Podium offered for contractors and field service businesses, especially considering how expensive the platform is. Overall, it has benefits, but there is definitely room for improvement, particularly for companies that work in the field all day rather than behind a desk.

text: We have been with Podium for 15 months now. Some things are great, and come as advertised. The AI will change its name, change the script, tell customers we offer things that we don’t, turn away customers for services we do offer, change the name of our company, etc etc. The list goes on and on. And no matter how many times we have complained and been promised that this would be resolved, the issues just continue to get worse. We are very disappointed in this, and are actively seeking to get away from the AI and back to an answering service. We are very tired and disappointed in the service and the support we have received on this aspect. We placed a lot of our eggs in this basket, and it is going to be a long, disappointing process to re-implement the old procedures to make up for what we were promised with Podium. I encourage anyone looking into an AI CSM to seek something else.

title: Append agent name to the message on WhatsApp channel
text: ### Is your feature or enhancement related to a problem? Please describe. Similar to #5855. Also, this type of stuff makes the CS process seem much more personal and tailored to the user, which is very important for every company. ### Describe the solution you'd like There should be an inbox option that appends the agent's name to the top of the message, or maybe a way to use templates, just like how canned responses work. So something like: ``` *{{agent.name}}*: {{message}} ``` ### Describe alternatives you've considered Right now, there are 2 alternatives: 1. using personal signatures: doesn't make sense on the WhatsApp channel, it's something you'd expect on an e-mail; 2. using canned responses: that would require typing / and selecting the response for every message they send, which is very counterintuitive. ### Additional context _No response_

title: PDC Management Suggestion - Full Feature [Bounty]
text: [![Bountysource](https://api.bountysource.com/badge/issue?issue_id=39242671)](https://www.bountysource.com/issues/39242671-pdc-management-suggestion-full-feature?utm_source=39242671&utm_medium=shield&utm_campaign=ISSUE_BADGE) Dear ALL, with reference to https://github.com/frappe/erpnext/issues/6859 , I think full feature required for managing PDCs are as follows:  FIELD TO BE ADDED IN JOURNAL/PAYMENT ENTRY • RECEIPT/VOUCHER DATE • DATE DEPOSITED (FOR PDCs RECEIVED)  In BANK RECONCILIATION, when bank account is not selected and the user clicked on “Get Payment Entries”, the Outstanding Cheques and Deposit in Transits for ALL Bank Accounts should be displayed based on the period covered selected. From there, user can update to which bank the cheque has been deposited (column for Deposited to - Bank Account Option). It should also automatically update entry to reclass the previously selected bank account during the initial entry when the cheque has been received. This is important to note since the company with different bank accounts have the discretion to which bank they want to deposit the cheque when it is due for deposit. This is also useful for companies receiving too many cheques in a day or a week in monitoring which cheques are still on hand awaiting for deposit. Update button should be added. In cases of Returned/Redeposited Cheques, there should also be a column in the Bank Reconciliation with label “Returned/Redeposited”. In the same way in entering when cheque was deposited, it should also automatically update reversal of initial entry on the journal (debiting back the receivable and crediting cash in bank for returned cheques / debiting back the cash in bank and crediting receivable for cheques redeposited)  FROM JOURNAL/PAYMENT ENTRY, A REPORT SAME AS THE BANK RECONCILIATION STATEMENT SHOULD BE GENERATED WITH THE FOLLOWING COLUMNS: • RECEIPT/VOUCHER DATE • POSTING DATE (SAME AS THE CHEQUE DATE) • PAYMENT ENTRY (Receipt/Voucher created ex. PDCR-00001, PDCI-00001, etc.) • AGAINST ACCOUNT (CUSTOMER/SUPPLIER, ETC.) • DEBIT AMOUNT • CREDIT AMOUNT • TOTAL FOR BOTH DEBIT AND CREDIT SIDE • CHEQUE/REFERENCE NO. • CHEQUE/REFERENCE DATE • DATE DEPOSITED / RETURNED • DEPOSITED TO (BANK ACCOUNT OPTION) NOTE: IN THIS REPORT, THERE SHOULD BE AN OPTION TO SELECT PERIOD COVERED FOR THE PERIOD WE WANT TO GENERATE  In connection to the above details, In CUSTOMER/SUPPLIER dashboard, below should be added aside from annual billing and total UNPAID (refers to invoices/returns only) Portion. PDCs RECEIVED BUT NOT YET CLEARED – this is to show how much PDCs were exactly received from the customer including uncleared cheques and paid to supplier including cheques date which have passed but not yet cleared in the bank. TOTAL OUTSTANDING - this portion does not only reflect invoices/returns made by customer/supplier but should also include journal entries made to book receivables/payables. This amount should not deduct uncleared cheques received/issued. NOTE: For most companies, not all users have the access to view GL to check how much PDC has been received/paid by customer or paid to supplier dashboard, in this case, we suggest to have this feature in viewing customer/supplier in ERPNext. Below is a sample for your reference: ![cus-](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/16744099/20304154/408e39e4-ab48-11e6-84a9-394f72d6fbe3.png) ![sup](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/16744099/20304162/48559550-ab48-11e6-90d6-a6592f300ca1.png)

title: Improving upon Item Price
text: We are buying and selling a lot of items of which the price varies based on quantity and customer or supplier that we buy from or sell to. Currently the only way this can be done is by pricing rules which we think are more to discount prices per customer or supplier group, time period (sales) etc. So in our mind using pricing rule to achieve quantity based pricing is a hack and not an ideal solution. We propose to improve upon Item Price by adding the fields: - Supplier (Link:Supplier) [if:buying] - Customer (Link:Customer) [if:selling] - Minimum Qty (Float) - UOM (Link: UOM) - Packing Unit (Int, quantity that must be bought or sold per UOM) - Rate per UOM (rename Rate to that to be specific) - Lead Time in days (Int) - Valid From (Date) - Valid Upto (Date) - Note (Text) - Disable (Checkbox) If this is possible then based on that also pricing rules can apply to further apply discounts etc. So for us we would put in 1-10 price breaks based on quantity for an item that we buy from up to 15 suppliers. title: bug: Incoming WhatsApp Cloud messages lost or delayed by hours (Self-hosted v4.10.1)
text: ### Describe the bug Incoming messages from WhatsApp Cloud API are either being lost or delivered with a massive delay (2 to 5 hours later). Outgoing messages work perfectly. This behavior started approximately a week ago without any changes to our infrastructure. Testing with a sequence of 20 numbered messages (1, 2, 3...), usually 2-3 messages never appear in the Chatwoot UI, and some arrive out of order hours later. Other channels like Telegram are working normally. ### To Reproduce 1. Setup a WhatsApp Cloud Inbox (tested on API v21.0, v22.0, v23.0 and v24.0). 2. Send a rapid sequence of 20 text messages (e.g., numbers 1 to 20) from a customer phone to the WhatsApp business number. 3. Observe the Chatwoot dashboard: 4. Some messages will skip (e.g., 1, 2, 4... missing 3). 5. Some messages appear hours later in the dashboard. 6. Check Sidekiq logs: Webhooks::WhatsappEventsJob shows the payload was received by Rails, but the job is often queued in low priority or processed out of order. ### Expected behavior All incoming webhooks from Meta should be processed in near real-time and displayed in the UI in the order they were sent, similar to how the Telegram channel performs. ### Environment Docker ### Cloud Provider Other [please specify in the description] ### Platform Browser ### Operating system Ubuntu 22.04 ### Browser and version Chrome ### Docker (if applicable) _No response_ ### Additional context Analysis of Logs: Rails logs show 200 OK for all Meta webhooks, meaning the server receives them. Meta API Changes: We suspect this is related to the recent implementation of Business-Scoped User IDs (BSUID) or Meta Portfolio Pacing (introduced/enforced in early 2026). Redundancy: Even after a fresh "from scratch" installation, the problem persists. Sidekiq Jobs: Logs show a high frequency of Notification::RemoveDuplicateNotificationJob, suggesting Chatwoot might be struggling with Meta's retry mechanism when a webhook is delayed. Community feedback: Several users in community groups are reporting the same "delayed or ghost messages" specifically for WhatsApp Cloud API starting Feb 2026.

title: [Feature] Customer and Supplier as one Party [Bounty]
text: [![Bountysource](https://api.bountysource.com/badge/issue?issue_id=41121617)](https://www.bountysource.com/issues/41121617-feature-suggestion-customer-and-supplier-as-one-party?utm_source=41121617&utm_medium=shield&utm_campaign=ISSUE_BADGE) In the real world of retail/wholesale business, most likely, some customers are also our suppliers. In this case, we are making invoices and bills for the same party… That is why is better to have just so called Party with the option to make it customer and supplier. In this case, for reconciliation purposes, supplier and customer Statement will be merged for the purpose of getting net of the actual payable or receivable for reconciliation as same in Odoo… But for reporting purposes, if invoices and bills are not yet paid, it still should be shown as separate accounts in the financial statements as payable(in liabilities section) and receivables (in asset section)… In getting the statement showing both balances of receivables and payables, there should be a button which can be used to offset amount with invoices and bill in case the party would want to pay only for the net outstanding balance for all invoices and bills. When clicking the button, it should automatically go to a journal entry wherein invoices and bills can be allocated to each other in order to allocate amounts which should take effect the offsetting of amounts to apply the receivables to payables and vice versa...

title: Database Changes and Optimisation
text: There are a few locations where the database can be cleaned up, and optimised slightly: 1. Redundant "surname" column in "contacts" table 2. Do not strictly need "has_kids" column, you can just query if "number of kids" > 0 3. Might be better to remove "number_of_reminders", etc. and query their respective tables and cache the result, then you don't need to store this information in multiple places. [Laravel's caching interface allows increment and decrement of these values.](https://laravel.com/docs/5.4/cache#cache-usage) 4. Could move the contact information (e.g. phone number) to its own table to solve #128. A `contact_type` and `contact_details` table, or something similar - this would work similar to how activities currently work. This would also allow the removal of the Twitter, FB, and LinkedIn profile links from the `users` table. 5. Column naming is strange in some places. Although you have a "currencies" table, in "gifts" there is a column named "value_in_dollars" - perhaps this should be currency agnostic? I have noticed this in the Monica front-end too. 6. In the 'activities' table the date column is named "date_it_happened" which presumes it happened in the past. Perhaps this should be changed to accommodate for #195 Just a few suggestions that might help optimise things! @djaiss - if you agree with any let me know and I might have some time to work on a PR - and congratulations on making such a useful piece of software! :)

title: Improve display of numerous relations - Implement 'show more' Overlay
text: # Current Behavior: Today, when there are too many relations, they are displayed without consideration of available space, leading to a cluttered appearance. ### Example issue on tasks: https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102394218/258555670-69f2c5c9-add6-45fc-ad88-cdc4c8b6374f.mp4 # Expected Behavior: The desired behavior is to apply a consistent display format for all multiple relations across the application. ### Proposed Solution: 1. Limiting Width Div: o When displaying relations, constrain them within a maximum width div. o The div should not exceed the length of a single line. 2. Displaying Maximum Elements: o Show the maximum number of relations that fit within the div. 3. Adding 'Show More' Indicator: o If the div is full and there are additional non-displayed relations, add a '+n' indicator, representing the number of hidden relations. 4. 'Show More' Interaction: o Make the '+n' indicator clickable. o When clicked, open an overlay that expands to the div's width and accommodates the content to display all the hidden relations. ### Example desired behavior on tasks: https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/102394218/258555611-b7dc316e-b028-4b35-b414-5bb7a3e21b7e.mp4 By implementing these changes, we aim to improve the display of numerous relations, ensuring a neat and organized presentation, and providing users with the option to access all relations via the 'Show More' overlay. ### Proposed implementation plan ```[tasklist] ### Tasks - [ ] Introduce a @/ui/OverflowingChipsWithTooltip component that take children as an argument and applying a width: 100% to itself - [ ] Add a useEffect to compute container size in js, compute estimated chip size based on text and icon - [ ] Add a +n button with remaining items - [ ] On click on the +n button, display a overflow div with the same width as it parent - [ ] On click outside, close the overflow div - [ ] Use this new component in Activity Right Panel, and on Task inbox ```

text: ## Describe the bug When sending media attachments (images, PDFs, audio) through WhatsApp Cloud API integration, messages fail intermittently with error `131053: Media upload error`. Text messages are delivered correctly 100% of the time. The issue started around **February 6, 2026** and is progressively getting worse, affecting thousands of self-hosted users. **The root cause is architectural.** Chatwoot currently sends media by providing a URL for Meta's servers to download. Meta's internal download service (fwdproxy) applies rate limiting based on the hosting provider's **ASN (Autonomous System Number)**, not per individual account. When many Chatwoot/Evolution API instances share the same hosting provider (e.g., Hostinger — ASN 47583), the aggregate download volume exceeds Meta's threshold and **all users on that provider are blocked intermittently**. The exact error from Meta's webhook: ``` Downloading media from weblink failed with http code 429, status message Too Many Requests, ratelimit reason: Request ratelimit by fwdproxy. Details: [GlobalCountingRatelimiter] Request hit ratelimit policy — destination matcher asn_list: 47583 ``` **This is not a temporary issue.** As Chatwoot adoption grows (especially in markets like Brazil where WhatsApp dominates), more providers will hit the same limit. The sustainable fix is to change media upload from URL-based to direct upload via `media_id`, which completely bypasses Meta's fwdproxy. ### Current flow (URL-based — causes the problem) ``` 1. User attaches file in Chatwoot 2. Chatwoot uploads file to storage (local/S3/MinIO) ✅ 3. Chatwoot sends file URL to WhatsApp API ✅ 4. Meta's fwdproxy tries to download file from user's server ❌ RATE LIMITED BY ASN 5. WhatsApp returns error 131053 ``` ### Proposed flow (direct upload via media_id — no fwdproxy involved) ``` 1. User attaches file in Chatwoot 2. Chatwoot uploads file to storage ✅ 3. Chatwoot uploads file directly to WhatsApp Media API → receives media_id ✅ 4. Chatwoot sends message referencing media_id ✅ 5. WhatsApp delivers media to recipient ✅ ``` This is how tools like n8n's WhatsApp node handle media — and they are not affected by this issue. ### Evidence - [[Discussion #13517](https://github.com/orgs/chatwoot/discussions/13517)](https://github.com/orgs/chatwoot/discussions/13517) — Multiple users reporting the same issue - Hostinger officially confirmed Meta is rate-limiting their ASN - Meta developer support confirmed the 429 is from fwdproxy's GlobalCountingRatelimiter targeting destination ASN - Users who migrated to providers with different ASNs report the issue disappears completely - The WhatsApp Cloud API officially supports both methods: [[URL-based](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/guides/send-messages#media-messages)](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/guides/send-messages#media-messages) and [[Direct upload](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/reference/media#upload-media)](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/reference/media#upload-media) ### To Reproduce ## To Reproduce 1. Deploy Chatwoot (any recent version) on a hosting provider with high Chatwoot/Evolution API density (e.g., Hostinger — ASN 47583) 2. Configure WhatsApp Cloud API inbox 3. Use any storage backend (local, S3-compatible, MinIO) — the issue occurs with all of them 4. Send a media attachment (image, PDF, or audio) to a WhatsApp contact 5. Observe that text messages are always delivered, but media fails intermittently with: ``` content_attributes: { "external_error" => "131053: Media upload error" } ``` 6. Check server logs — the file is uploaded to storage successfully: ``` S3 Storage (36.9ms) Uploaded file to key: 488mr7jp78rvfayn4m2suyagxa4l ``` 7. But the Active Storage serves it via redirect: ``` Processing by ActiveStorage::Blobs::RedirectController#show as PDF Redirected to https://storage.example.com/chatwoot/488mr7jp...?X-Amz-Expires=300&X-Amz-Signature=... Completed 302 Found in 19ms ``` 8. Meta's fwdproxy attempts to download from the redirect URL, hits the ASN rate limit, and returns 429 **Important:** The failure is intermittent because it depends on the aggregate traffic volume from all Chatwoot instances on the same ASN at that moment. It fails more during business hours (high traffic) and works more often at night (low traffic). **Environment:** - Chatwoot version: Multiple versions affected (tested on 4.10.1 and others) - Channel: WhatsApp Cloud API (official) - Storage: Tested with S3-compatible (MinIO) and local disk — same result - Docker version: Docker Engine 24.x / 28.x - OS: Ubuntu 24.04 ### Expected behavior ## Expected behavior Media attachments should be delivered reliably to WhatsApp contacts regardless of the hosting provider's ASN or aggregate traffic from other Chatwoot instances. **Proposed implementation:** 1. **Primary:** Chatwoot should upload media files directly to the WhatsApp Cloud API media endpoint (`POST /{phone_number_id}/media`), receive a `media_id`, and send the message using `"document": {"id": "media_id"}` instead of `"document": {"link": "https://..."}`. This completely eliminates the dependency on Meta's fwdproxy and makes media sending immune to ASN-based rate limiting. 2. **Alternative:** If a full migration is not immediately feasible, add a configurable option: ``` WHATSAPP_MEDIA_UPLOAD_STRATEGY=direct # "direct" for media_id upload, "link" for current behavior ``` This approach would also fix the related issue where Active Storage's 302 redirects cause `131053` errors due to WhatsApp not following redirects properly (returning `Unsupported mime type text/html` instead of the actual file). ### Environment Docker ### Cloud Provider Other [please specify in the description] ### Platform Browser ### Operating system Ubuntu 22.04 ### Browser and version Chrome Latest ### Docker (if applicable) _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

title: Double consecutive `createView` calls may cause side effects
text: **Describe the bug** Double consecutive `createView` calls may cause side effects (dangling promises) because of the way Bullbone works. Most often such an error is related to double consecutive re-render (closely related to https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/issues/2635) or `prepare` call. **Explanation** Suppose (i) a view _A_ that creates nested view _B_ inside its `prepare` function. For example A = `time-ranges` and B = `item-detail` of working calendar field, which already exist in EspoCRM. Suppose (ii) that view B takes some time to load. We can simulate this by adding ```js this.wait(new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 500))); ``` to its setup function. (I couldn't find a view in Espo that meets both conditions (i) and (ii), but developers can create such views. For sake of this example I appended the `wait` line to the `item-detail` manually). Now: 1. Begin inline editation of view _A_ 2. Make changes 3. **Close** inline editation https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/6afd616e42deb6ec9f9590803fd1825fc28c01a5/client/src/views/fields/base.js#L1280-L1286 4. This causes a call to `setDetailMode` function, which calls `prepare`. This creates a promise _X_ on which depends the correct termination of inline editation. 5. Initial attributes are stored back to model, which causes change event. Causing another call to `prepare`. 6. Another call to `prepare` marks promise _X_ as cancelled. However, as view _B_ takes some time to load, promise _X_ haven't resolved yet. 7. This creates dangling promise _X_, thus inline editation never terminates correctly and editation links never disappear. I think that this is fundamental issue with Bullbone, as developes have no feedback when createView terminates. I can think of adding a new option to `createView`, that tells `createView` to reject, when promise is marked as cancelled. ```diff delete this._viewPromiseHash[key]; if (promise && promise._isToCancel) { + if (options.rejectOnCancel) { + reject(); + } return; } ```

title: Add an option to confirm email address on signup
text: Europe is launching a new law in May, called GDPR, which is great, but comes with a lot of constraints for anyone having a webservice. One of the thing we need to do to be compliant is: _With e-mail double opt-in, a new user first needs to verify their e-mail address before completing the sign-up process._ I've tried to prevent doing this on Monica since the beginning - not because I wanted to collect your email address and do nasty thing with it, but because I wanted people to sign up with fake email addresses if they wanted to. This law will force us to confirm email addresses on signup. We will create a new `.env` variable, called `SIGNUP_DOUBLE_OPTIN`, which will default to `TRUE`. On our hosted version, it will be set to true, but you will do whatever you want on your own instance. Note: to be clear, we do have an email newsletter, but we only contact people who have subscribed manually and specifically to receive this newsletter. The email address used on signup is never used otherwise, other than sending reminder emails. Changes to do: - [ ] Create a email confirmation process - [ ] Keep track of when the user has validated his email address - [ ] Display this information in the Settings panel under a new section (called `Compliance`) - [ ] Add a method in the User object, something like `isCompliant`, that will tell if users have confirmed emails and accepted Terms & Privacy. If not, we should block email sending (reminders, notifications,...) automatically. This will be done in https://github.com/monicahq/monica/issues/1184 so you don't have to do it here. cc @asbiin @Mokto

title: development QoL improvements
text: I'm a big fan of this CRM system due to its flexibility and well thought design, already used it for several business and private projects. However, the workflow of frontend and extension development is not optimal in my opinion for the reasons described below. I would like to discuss those, whether you are willing to address these and get feedback about the proposals. > [!NOTE] > I'm ready and willing to provide the implementation of the proposals (or other solutions) by myself, so this is not meant as feature request but rather as discussion of the aspects. If you agree with my perspective/solutions I will split this issue to feature requests and provide the implementations as PRs. # 1. issues ## 1. extensions layout **Motivation**: As a developer I want to be able to work on multiple extensions at the same time on the same base install of EspoCRM. This enables appropriate debugging and testing of extensions which built a unified crm and may even depend on another. I developed a containerized development stack to address this issue but it relies on hacks that might break in future releases. **Issue**: Since the extension files are split into 3 locations (`custom/Espo/Modules`, `client/custom/modules` and `data/upload/extensions`) installing them requires some kind of mapping/bundling (as the [ext-template] does). This adds complexity to the development workflow and makes it hard to manage multi-extension development environments (especially within containers where symlinks are a common source of error) whereas I can't see a benefit of that structure. **Solution**: Create a single root directory for extensions where each sub-folder contains the necessary files of one extension. This allows to clone the extension repo into the root directory and directly work with that. ## 2. library/package management **Motivation**: As a developer I want to be able to install composer and npm libraries and expect them to integrate without further configuration/build setups. **Issues**: 1. bundling composer libraries requires creation of `autoload.json` and handle to copy the `vendor` folder 2. bundling npm libraries is not supported as of now and requires lots of efforts (copy the libraries files, possibly transpile them, add the libraries to json config, ...) **Solution**: 1. define a default location of the `vendor` directory and make `autoload.json` optional. 2. extend (or replace) current Transpiler and Bundler to support importing modules from `node_modules` inside ESM ## 3. development workflow **Motivation**: As a developer I want to focus on the development and not the build workflow, thus I would highly appreciate file watchers and hot-reloading (of frontend js/css) which can drastically reduce development time. **Issue**: Currently there are no file watchers/hot-reloading in the main repository, neither for [ext-template]. By applying the refactoring mentioned in [1. folder structure/mapping](#1-folder-structure-mapping), implementing file watchers and hot-reloading in the main espocrm repository could also handle extensions aswell. # 2. proposals These are my approaches to solve the issues of described in 1. They are not fully thought-out but rather define a basis of how it could be implemented. ## 1. refactor extensions layout To solve issue 1.1. and prepare handling 1.2. and 1.3. I propose to define a new extensions root folder **Key aspects**: - common root extensions folder - support installed (compiled and bundled) and development ("raw" repository) extensions - (optional) compact layout (reduce file path lengths) **Considerations**: - how to handle crm module - how to handle update migration - which hardcoded paths exist and is it possible to migrate them automatically (eg `autoload.json`) - development of extensions with old layout is hard to integrate (though using the existing build scripts form [ext-template] would be still possible) Proposed extension layout production development why? ``` espocrm/ ├─ extensions/ │ ├─ bundled-extension/ │ │ ├─ app/ │ │ │ ├─ Resources/ │ │ │ │ ├─ module.json │ │ ├─ client/ │ │ │ ├─ lib/ │ │ │ ├─ res/ │ │ │ ├─ src/ │ │ ├─ hooks/ │ │ │ ├─ AfterInstall.php │ │ ├─ vendor/ │ │ ├─ manifest.json ``` ``` espocrm/ ├─ extensions/ │ ├─ dev-extension/ │ │ ├─ app/ │ │ │ ├─ Resources/ │ │ │ │ ├─ module.json │ │ ├─ client/ │ │ │ ├─ lib/ │ │ │ ├─ res/ │ │ │ ├─ src/ │ │ ├─ hooks/ │ │ │ ├─ AfterInstall.php │ │ ├─ tests/ │ │ │ ├─ integration/ │ │ │ ├─ unit/ │ │ ├─ vendor/ │ │ ├─ node_modules/ │ │ ├─ extension.json │ │ ├─ composer.json │ │ ├─ package.json ``` - common root folder for extensions (which makes multi-extension dev setup easier) - self-contained, single root folders for extensions - developer-friendly extension layout - espocrm in developer mode enables extensions that have `extension.json` instead of `manifest.json` at their root folder - reduce development build complexity (only run compilers/transpilers) - enables root-level file watchers from espocrm main repository (instead of watching every extension on its own) - backwards compatibility - map folders from previous layout: - `app` -> `files/custom/Espo/Modules/ ` - `client` -> `files/client/custom/modules/ ` - `hooks` -> `scripts/` - `app/Resources/autoload.json` is optional, defaulting to `vendor/` - no need to adjust code for old extension layout, mapping folders to new layout on installation ## 2. refactor build tool To solve the issues described in 1.2. the following changes are required: 1. include `extensions/ /vendor` if present, additional look at `extensions/ /app/Resources/autoload.json` for backwards compatibility 2. bundling npm libraries (adjust Transpiler to create a list of imports from `node_modules` and use Bundler to add them to the build?) Additionaly, to support 1.3. it is necessary to: 3. implement watch task in grunt (possibly using [grunt-contrib-watch](https://github.com/gruntjs/grunt-contrib-watch#optionslivereload)) - watching on `espocrm/client` to transpile and bundle js/css/templates for espocrm - watching on `client` folder of every extension in `espocrm/extensions` to transpile and bundle js/css/templates for extensions I want to throw in the possibility to move to an external build tool (like vite, webpack, ...) which support those features with less expense and possibly helps new developers to customize the build workflow for their extensions. However I'm aware this is a big change and beside the initial cost of migration (which I would definitely love to provide if interested exists) it is also a choice of flavor and experience. title: Provide a demo environment
text: ## Scope & Context We don't really have a good way to demo the app for someone who wouldn't want to signup. We need better seeding data and a way to reset automatically the content if it's modified. ## Periodic reset endpoint Create an env variable DEMO_WORKSPACES which will hold an an array of ids. Create a new mutation ResetDemo on the API that takes an id as parameters. We'll setup a service like uptimerobot to update this frequently. That operation should: - check it's really a demo account, as per the env variable - the if check is ok: - clear existing people, companies, opportunities, ... - create new ones from seed files Then, on the backend, prevent the following actions from being executed if the workspace is in DEMO_WORKSPACES: - Creating an API Key - Deleting an API Key - Deleting the Workspace - Inviting a member ## Improve seed data We already have 2 ways to generate seed data: (1) files in database/seeds/ which contains seed data for a dev environment. Maybe in the future can me improved to be generated with a library like faker (2) files in src/core/{object}/seed-date/{object}.json those are just a few items, they are real people/companies and are meant to avoid throwing people into an empty workspace. It's just a few items that are meant to look nice and be deleted when you start using the CRM. We need to create a third dataset, that will be very similar to (2), i.e. nice looking/real companies, but with a lot more records (500 companies + 500 people + 100 opportunities would be nice) I recommend created a second .json file and using ChatGPT Code Interpreter to generate these files. We want these companies to feel relatable so maybe use a list of S&P 500 Companies or something like that as an initial input in ChatGPT Code Interpreter. They shouldn't be fake companies. ## Pre-fill sign-in There is already an environment variable to pre-fill the login form. It's helpful to pre-fill the login on non-production environment but doesn't help us in the production environment. We would need to be able to overwrite isSignInPrefilled based on a url parameter. e.g. app.twenty.com?demo=true or any other similar suitable format

title: Import should use bulk insert
text: Currently, import uses saveEntity which creates single row insert at a time. ## Problem If I am importing say 100,000 `lead`, for example, which contains `emailAddresses` and `phoneNumbers` - 100,000 insert queries to insert lead - 100,000 insert queries to insert emailAddresses - 100,000 insert queries to insert phoneNumbers - 100,000 insert queries to insert entity_email_address - 100,000 insert queries to insert entity_phone_numbers Total of 500,000 insert queries are needed to be run ignoring the inserts for process history records, relations etc... This makes import painfully slow. My research on speed on inserts is here: https://stackoverflow.com/a/57452308 Proposed: Use bulk insert with multiple rows Example, ```sql Insert into `lead` (first_name, last_name) values ('a', 'b'), -- row 1 ('c', 'd'), -- row 2 ('e', 'f'); -- row 3 ``` For bulk update use `case` keyword. Example, ```sql update `lead` set first_name = ( CASE id WHEN '5f232342d' THEN 'a' WHEN '243242dsf' THEN 'b' END ) WHERE id IN ('5f232342d', '243242dsf'); ``` FYI, you need to think about how `beforeSave`, `afterSave` and hooks will work also

title: Email replies not being tracked (possible fix using imap_fetch_overview instead of imap_search)
text: What type of report is this: Bug Report ## Description: Emails are not tracking in mautic. PHP Version: PHP 7.0.27 (cli) (built: Feb 17 2018 01:53:37) ( NTS ) Copyright (c) 1997-2017 The PHP Group Zend Engine v3.0.0, Copyright (c) 1998-2017 Zend Technologies Mautic version: 2.12.2 ### Steps to reproduce: 1. Setup IMAP for a gsuite account 2. Make sure you have replies in your tracked folder 3. Run the command: `php /var/www/html/app/console mautic:email:fetch` Result: `0 emails processed for {imap.gmail.com:993/imap/ssl}INBOX with a criteria of UID 20:*` Expected: `2 emails processed` I've done a lot of digging and I believe that it comes down to one simple issue: usage of php's `imap_search()` function in the `searchMailbox` function of the `Mailbox.php` class as seen here: https://github.com/mautic/mautic/blob/staging/app/bundles/EmailBundle/MonitoredEmail/Mailbox.php#L559. If you notice, the criteria outputted by the logging for the fetch command is `UID 20:*`. From what I can tell, this isn't supported by php's `imap_search()` function: http://php.net/manual/en/function.imap-search.php. It isn't in the list of criteria, and I tested it extensively, with many variations in the php interactive console. I was able to get messages via the "all" command, and several others, but not with the undocumented "UID" command. I did have success with `imap_fetch_overview()` http://php.net/manual/en/function.imap-fetch-overview.php, however. I propose that we use `imap_search()` for searches, and `imap_fetch_overview()` for uid range-based lookups.

title: Feature Request: Integrate WhatsApp Cloud API for Groups
text: ### Is your feature or enhancement related to a problem? Please describe. Yes, this feature is related to a problem. Currently, Chatwoot's WhatsApp Cloud API integration only supports 1-to-1 conversations. Many business use cases, especially in support, sales, and coordination, require multi-party conversations. For example: Complex Support: A customer has an issue that requires both a support agent and a technical specialist (or an external vendor/installer) to be in the same chat. High-Value Sales: A sales agent needs to coordinate with a client and their manager or a finance person in a single thread. Travel/Events: An agency needs to create a small group chat for a family or a couple to discuss booking details. Right now, the only way to handle this is for the agent to talk to the customer, then talk to their colleague in a private note or separate channel, and then relay the information back. This is slow, inefficient, and lacks transparency for the customer. We are forced to use personal WhatsApp accounts for group chats, which means the conversations are not tracked in Chatwoot. ### Describe the solution you'd like I would like Chatwoot to integrate the new WhatsApp Cloud API for Groups, as documented by Meta here: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/cloud-api/groups This integration should allow agents to: Create new groups: An agent should be able to initiate a new WhatsApp Group conversation from the Chatwoot dashboard. Invite participants: The agent should be able to send a group invite link to the primary contact and add other participants (like other agents or external phone numbers) to the chat. Manage group conversations: These new group chats should appear in the inbox just like 1-to-1 chats, but clearly marked as a "group". Send & Receive Messages: All agents and contacts in the group should be able to send and receive messages, media, and templates within that single conversation thread, with all history saved in Chatwoot. Use Webhooks: The integration should listen for group webhooks (e.g., group_participants_update) so the chat updates in real-time if a user joins or leaves. This would allow us to handle multi-party case resolutions directly within Chatwoot, keeping all communication centralized, tracked, and professional. ### Describe alternatives you've considered _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

title: WhatsApp Business-Scoped User IDs (BSUID) support needed before June 2026
text: ## Summary Meta is launching [WhatsApp Usernames](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-scoped-user-ids) — users will be able to set an `@username` and **hide their phone number** from businesses. To support this, Meta is adding a **Business-Scoped User ID (BSUID)** to all webhook payloads via a new `user_id` field. **Starting June 2026**, the `wa_id` / `from` fields that currently always contain a phone number **may contain a BSUID instead** (format: `CC.alphanumeric`, e.g. `BR.1A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9I0J...`). This will break Chatwoot's contact resolution for username-adopting users. ## Timeline | Date | What happens | |------|-------------| | Early April 2026 | Contact Book feature — Meta auto-stores phone+BSUID pairs from prior interactions | | May 2026 | BSUIDs start appearing in **all** webhook payloads (testing phase) | | **June 2026** | Usernames launch in test countries — `wa_id` may be BSUID, not phone | | August 2026+ | Global rollout | ## What breaks in Chatwoot Chatwoot currently uses the phone number (`wa_id`) as the primary identifier for WhatsApp contacts: 1. **`Whatsapp::IncomingMessageBaseService`** resolves contacts via `wa_id` assuming it's always a phone number 2. **`ContactInbox`** uses `source_id` (phone number in E.164) with a unique index on `(inbox_id, source_id)` 3. **`find_or_create_contact`** maps phone number → Contact record When a username-adopting user messages a business and their phone number is **not** in the Contact Book: - `wa_id` / `from` will be a BSUID, not a phone number - Chatwoot will create a **duplicate contact** (new `source_id` with the BSUID) instead of matching the existing contact - Sending replies may fail if the code assumes `wa_id` is always E.164 ## Webhook payload changes **New field `user_id`** — always present in all message webhooks (regardless of username adoption): ```json { "contacts": [{"profile": {"name": "Jessica"}, "wa_id": "BR.1A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9I0J..."}], "messages": [{ "from": "BR.1A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9I0J...", "user_id": "BR.1A2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9I0J...", "id": "wamid.xxx", "type": "text", "text": {"body": "Hello"} }] } ``` For users **without** usernames, `wa_id` remains a phone number, but `user_id` (BSUID) is still present. ## Suggested approach 1. **Store `user_id` (BSUID)** — add a `bsuid` / `whatsapp_user_id` column to `ContactInbox` or `Contact` 2. **Dual-key contact resolution** — match by BSUID first, fall back to phone number, write BSUID back when matched by phone 3. **Detect BSUID vs phone** — BSUIDs have the format `CC.alphanum` (2-letter country code + dot + up to 128 chars), phone numbers are E.164 4. **Handle sending to BSUIDs** — when no phone number is known, use the BSUID as the recipient identifier in the Cloud API ## References - [Meta: Business-Scoped User IDs](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-scoped-user-ids) - [Twilio: BSUID field required June 2026](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/whatsapp-usernames--new-business-scoped-user-id--bsuid--field-re) - [WABetaInfo: Official update on usernames and BSUIDs](https://wabetainfo.com/whatsapp-shares-official-update-on-usernames-and-business-scoped-ids-ahead-of-2026-deadline/) ## Environment - Self-hosted Chatwoot CE (latest) - WhatsApp Cloud API with coexistence mode - Affects all WhatsApp Cloud API integrations I'm happy to contribute a PR if the team can provide guidance on the preferred approach for contact resolution changes.

title: Recurring Campaigns / Repeating Tasks
text: [Feature request] In a campaign, if a lead triggers action "Change Campaigns -> Remove Lead From -> This Campaign" then the lead's "track record" of actions, decisions and conditions from this given campaign gets nullified. If the lead now gets added to the source of this campaign again, it starts campaign afresh. This will allow recurring campaigns or re-using the campaign repeatedly, based on condition. At present, actions inside campaigns run only once. This prevents campaigns to work as recurrent ones, a lead can't re-use the same campaign logic path from the beginning, if it has already passed through this campaign path. The lack of this functionality has been mentioned [here](https://www.mautic.org/community/index.php/1523-recurring-campaign-scheduler) and [here](https://www.mautic.org/community/index.php/1012-campaign-does-not-restart). Does this sound like a realistic feature to implement? There are many use cases like repeating follow-up emails (every time a person buys an item), routine reminder letters (like "we never ask you for a password"), recurring account maintenance checks ("please update your account info"), repeating on-action "thank you letters", on-action confirmation letters, basically, any condition-based or smart list-based recurring task. I think it can not be implemented with the present Mautic functionality, correct me please if there is a workaround. Otherwise, big thank you for your work and congrats with Mautic success!

On the other hand if they can be modified from the tag editor. In the case of group accounts, very few labels / fields can be translated (they are not in the PO file). What strikes me is that I already have them in Spanish (?) * ![0005](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/110789/33528936-fd194d60-d847-11e7-8ded-490a145411e6.png) * ![0005b](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/110789/33528937-fd432e6e-d847-11e7-91a9-23e1e2b77b7d.png) * ![0006](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/110789/33528938-fd66232e-d847-11e7-8be5-d91df110a3e4.png) * ![0006b](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/110789/33528939-fd87d50a-d847-11e7-9ae1-2a314cb706f8.png) 4. I do not know why this happens but it would be interesting if the new terms remain blank, this helps us identify them and translate them faster. Finally I want to thank all the work they do. It is a great CRM. I do not want this thing that I write to bother anyone, it's just my contribution. Let me know when you update the terms in POEditor so I finish the translations. Regards! Mauricio.

title: Docker instance behind reverse proxy uses incorrect App Url
text: ## Problem I'm trying to run an instance of MonicaHQ via Docker and behind a reverse proxy (Caddy), but when using the domain name I created for the app, it uses the wrong URL when getting resources. ## Context I created a subdomain like crm.domain.com that points to my server address. There, I have a Caddy instance in a Docker container that proxies requests from that subdomain to the IP of the MonicaHQ Docker container. This part works fine for the most part, as when I navigate to crm.domain.com in my browser I'm greeted by a semi-broken login page. The reason the login page is broken is that Monica is making requests to the Docker container IP instead of the App URL I set in the .env. I.e. instead of going to https://crm.domain.com/css/... it's going to http://172.17.0.6/css/... This breaks 1) because a https domain is trying to load http resources and 2) because 172.17.0.6 is the local IP of the Docker container on my server and is not publicly accessible. ## Attempted Fixes I pulled down the Monica source and modified `scripts/docker/000-default.conf` to set the ServerName directive, then tried building the container and running. That still didn't work as I saw the httpd warning about it unable to figure out the domain name and using 172.17.0.6 as the backup. I then exec'd into the running container and modified `/etc/apache2/httpd.conf` and set the ServerName directive there. When running `httpd` from inside the container, it would no longer show the error about ServerName not being set. However, the issue persists. I also tried setting `APP_TRUSTED_PROXIES=*` in my .env but still no dice. Any ideas on where to go from here?

title: =?UTF-8?Q? in e-mail headers
text: **Describe the bug** When sending e-mails, Espo is adding =?UTF-8?Q? and other non-printable characters into 'From' and 'Subject' fields of the header. **To Reproduce** 1. Send an e-mail via formula or via 'Send Test Email' button 2. Look at headers of received e-mail **Expected behavior** The e-mail header fields from and subject should contain plain characters as long as no special non-utf8/ascii characters have been entered by the user. **Actual behavior** 1. The issue only affects the 'from' field when you set a 'from name' in Espo. 3. The issue seems to affect the subject as well (regardless whether 'from name' is filled or not) 4. The behavior does not depend on special characters in the 'from name'. Using a simple one like 'asd' also causes it, please see screenshots. 5. [not an important issue, but noticed during testing] If you enter a 'from name' in outbound settings, then save, then reload the page, then delete the contents of the 'from name' field, then click 'Send Test Email', the system still sends the 'from name' you had before **Screenshots** E-Mail addresses have been hidden. They are correct though and do not contain faulty characters. ![utf8_from](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/assets/43390818/b7c3904e-f1b8-4d56-9d75-4e6d39e1da36) 'from name' has been set​ ![simple_from](https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/assets/43390818/8a153be0-fc8e-45cf-8785-c7f0e9b29b83) no 'from name' has been set **EspoCRM version** 8.0.4 **Additional context** I have replied to another user in the forum who seems to have the same issue but I think my post there might not be very visible. https://forum.espocrm.com/forum/general/78024-cryptic-from-sender-in-e-mails ​I think the words have somehow been double or unnecessarily encoded. This will trigger some spam guards as this technique is sometimes used by spammers. If I understand correctly (but please don't quote me on it ), the email currently does not follow strict RFC5322 standards https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5322#section-3.4 An improvement might be to only perform the current encoding if non-standard-ASCII characters are encountered. A few possibly useful links: https://security.stackexchange.com/a/213477 https://stackoverflow.com/a/55210089 ​I think the issue might occur here (haven't debugged yet though) https://github.com/espocrm/espocrm/blob/master/application/Espo/Core/Mail/Sender.php#L569​

title: "To" addresses are lost in Email Inboxes when replying via Chatwoot UI
text: # Description If Chatwoot receives an email like this: ``` From: john@aaa.test To: support@mycompany.example.com, jane@aaa.test Cc: jill@aaa.test ``` then when an agent replies in Chatwoot, the response email will only be delivered to `john@aaa.test` and `jill@aaa.test`, and it won't be delivered to `jane@aaa.test`. This is a common scenario for us, and it results in frustration when people get dropped off the email chain. I believe this is due to this javascript code: https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/blob/608592db0c11db142c9a281d1d34b715ad33d6c0/app/javascript/dashboard/components/widgets/conversation/ReplyBox.vue#L1122-L1148 The `to` variable in that code only gets set in a very particular case and is usually dropped. # Potential Solutions ### Option A: Add "To" addresses to the CC field in the editor UPDATE: @pranavrajs [confirmed that](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/8925#issuecomment-1961997686) we should go with this option. Update the above code to add each address in `emailAttributes.to` to the `cc` variable, **except** when the address is: * The Inbox email address (e.g. `support@mycompany.example.com` in the example above) * A reply email address (e.g. `reply+xxx@mycompany.example.com`) * The current conversation contact's email ### ~Option B: Add a "To" field in the message editor and populate it.~ UPDATE: We want to go with the other option. The message editor only has "CC" and "BCC" fields. Add another field to the editor for "To" addresses. Evaluate the addresses in `emailAttributes.to` as described in Option A, but add any relevant addresses to `to` instead of `cc`. We should ensure the current conversation contact's email is in either `to` or `cc`, or else I believe [this code](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/blob/cb2b75ca17db51f2eaefdafbb349b2ad31b87500/app/mailers/conversation_reply_mailer.rb#L186-L189) will cause the conversation contact to not receive the email. We should also be mindful of [this code](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/blob/608592db0c11db142c9a281d1d34b715ad33d6c0/app/javascript/dashboard/components/widgets/conversation/ReplyBox.vue#L1133-L1138) and make sure that scenario is still handled correctly. # Other notes/requirements We should add tests covering any new or updated behavior, and covering existing behavior if we don't have tests for that already. ### Environment Linux VM ### Platform Browser

title: WhatsApp Embedded Signup fails with "No WABA scope found in token" error (TokenValidationService)
text: ### Describe the bug When attempting to create a new WhatsApp inbox using Embedded Signup, the process fails with a 422 error containing "No WABA scope found in token", even though the Meta App has all required permissions configured (whatsapp_business_management, whatsapp_business_messaging). The issue is in TokenValidationService which expects whatsapp_business_management in the granular_scopes array returned by Meta's /debug_token endpoint, but Meta is returning business_management instead. Error in Rails logs: [WHATSAPP DEBUG] Token debug data: {"data"=>{"app_id"=>"...", "type"=>"USER", "application"=>"...", "is_valid"=>true, "scopes"=>["whatsapp_business_management", "whatsapp_business_messaging", "business_management", "public_profile"], "granular_scopes"=>[ {"scope"=>"business_management"}, {"scope"=>"whatsapp_business_manage_events"} ], ...}} [WHATSAPP] Token validation failed: No WABA scope found in token Notice that: scopes array correctly contains whatsapp_business_management granular_scopes array contains business_management (not whatsapp_business_management) granular_scopes entries have no target_ids field Root Cause Analysis The TokenValidationService (around line 30-45) does the following validation: rubywaba_scope = granular_scopes.find { |s| s['scope'] == 'whatsapp_business_management' } raise 'No WABA scope found in token' if waba_scope.blank? target_ids = waba_scope['target_ids'] || [] raise "Token does not have access to WABA #{@waba_id}" unless target_ids.include?(@waba_id) This fails because: Meta returns business_management instead of whatsapp_business_management in granular_scopes Even if we fallback to business_management, the target_ids array is empty [] This appears to be a change in Meta's API behavior. The [Meta documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/embedded-signup/manage-accounts/) shows whatsapp_business_management with target_ids, but the actual API response differs. ### To Reproduce To Reproduce Self-hosted Chatwoot v4.12.1 Configure WhatsApp Embedded Signup with: WHATSAPP_APP_ID WHATSAPP_CONFIGURATION_ID WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET WHATSAPP_API_VERSION=v25.0 Meta App configured with permissions: whatsapp_business_management, whatsapp_business_messaging Navigate to Settings → Inboxes → Add Inbox → WhatsApp Click "Connect with WhatsApp Business" Complete the Facebook authentication flow Select WhatsApp Business Account and phone number Error: 422 Unprocessable Entity - "No WABA scope found in token" ### Expected behavior The Embedded Signup should complete successfully since: The token IS valid (is_valid: true) The token DOES have the required scopes in the scopes array The Embedded Signup flow itself already validates WABA access ### Environment Docker ### Cloud Provider Other [please specify in the description] ### Platform Browser ### Operating system Ubuntu (Docker container) ### Browser and version Chrome (latest) / Safari ### Docker (if applicable) Chatwoot v4.12.1 (chatwoot/chatwoot:v4.12.1) Docker version: 24.x or later ### Additional context ## The Bug When creating a new WhatsApp inbox via Embedded Signup, the process fails with 422 error: "No WABA scope found in token" ## Root Cause `TokenValidationService` expects `whatsapp_business_management` in `granular_scopes`, but Meta's `/debug_token` API now returns `business_management` instead, with empty `target_ids`. **Actual API response:** - `scopes`: ["whatsapp_business_management", "whatsapp_business_messaging", "business_management"] ✅ - `granular_scopes`: [{"scope": "business_management"}, {"scope": "whatsapp_business_manage_events"}] ❌ (no whatsapp_business_management, no target_ids) ## Workaround Modified `TokenValidationService` to: 1. Check `scopes` array instead of `granular_scopes` 2. Accept `business_management` OR `whatsapp_business_management` 3. Skip `target_ids` verification (Embedded Signup already validates WABA access) ## Additional Issue `WHATSAPP_API_VERSION` not passed to frontend - `dashboard_controller.rb` missing the key in `app_config`, causing frontend to default to v22.0. ## Environment Details - Chatwoot: v4.12.1 - WhatsApp API Version: v25.0 - Meta App: Production mode with all required permissions - 14 existing WhatsApp inboxes work fine, only NEW inbox creation fails

text: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** EspoCRM is very versatile and can be used far beyond CRM (as demonstrated in sales pack and other extensions alike). For example: Warehouse Goods Issue, once processed shouldn't be touched in any way as it's an accounting document. Also in addition to this an option where administrator can override the lock would be helpful. **Describe alternatives you've considered** You can lock the records from being edited with before save hook, however this solution is not very versatile and user editable. Dynamic logic can also be applied to make field read only, by setting it for each field, but it's not convenient for future changes, or even setting up and still if adjustment is needed (from CRM admin) the admin would need to edit the dynamic logic beforehand. **Additional context** I saw this feature when I tried vtiger cloud demo and while espocrm definetely beats vtiger, I beleive this feature would be useful to have in core Espo.

title: Exclude user's email address from CC list when replying to emails
text: **Describe the bug** When you reply to an email ~from a Group Email Account~ where you're CC'd, your own email address gets added to the CC list again, even though it's already correctly set in the "From" field. **Steps to reproduce the behavior:** 1. Set up EspoCRM with a Group Email Account and a Personal Email Account. 2. Send an email: - Address it to the Group Email Account (in the "TO" field). - Include the user's Personal Email Account in the CC list. 3. Log in as the user associated with the Personal Email Account. 4. Reply to the email. 5. Notice that in the reply: - The "FROM" address correctly shows the Personal Email Account. - However, the CC list still includes the user's own email address from the Personal Email Account, despite being the sender. This issue arises because the system doesn't filter out the sender's own email address from the CC list when generating the reply, leading to redundancy in email recipients. **Expected behavior** When a user replies to an email: - The "From" address should correctly reflect the user's email address. - The CC list should not include the user's own email address, even if it was included in the original email's CC list. **EspoCRM version** 8.3.5 **Possible solutions** 1. Modify the code to filter out the user's primary email address from the CC list. ```js attributes.cc = (model.get('cc') || '').split(';').filter(item => { return item !== this.getUser().get('emailAddress'); }); ``` 2. Ensure that an email address in the "CC" list cannot be the same as the email address in the "FROM" field.

title: Project bigger than what was initially planned. How to tell the customer the higher price and different contract conditions?
text: I agreed with a customer to import data from excel files and build a report with them. Since it was not a big project I did not charge too much. I also asked for an annual fee for bug fixing and maintenance. As in the boiling frog story , the customer asked for little changes now and then (the frog is me). After more than a year I realized that I'd built a sort of ERP, where importing excel data was used only once to avoid the initial manual data entry phase. In order to get the report, I had implemented (for free) a lot of business logic and many statistical calculations just to have a "correct" model (bespoke to the customer). I'd like to give to my customer a new version of the contract I use for ERP programs (and not for import/export utilities as I did with him), with higher prices for the initial software cost, annual maintenance and other contract conditions. The project is nearly completed. How can I tell all of this to the customer? I'm afraid he could reply "Hey, we have agreed to this price, I'll pay you only that. The changes you made are part of annual maintanence after all". And as I managed the things he wouldn't be completely wrong. I'd like just to try to recover the situation if possible. Thanks for your help. Update - 7th July 2017 I followed the advise to list all the extra features, but the customer kept changing point of view just to be right whatever I said. After sending him a copy of old e-mails to show how his mind (hem...) was not serving him well, he started to say he has an intellectual property on the calculations (it's a weighted average that I suggest to use...). I offered him the option to pay me nothing more, keeping the part of software he payed, but he had to delete my software (the part not payed) otherwise he was infringing my copyright. I sent also a license agreement. He never answered. After that, I talk with a lawyer, a friend of mine, who offered to send him an order for payment just to unblock the situation. title: Credit card issued against my express refusal; What action can I take?
text: About a year ago, I walked into my local Wells Fargo branch, where I have several personal and business accounts. I had several transactions to take care of and I asked the banker to be quick because I had an international flight to catch. Despite my request, the banker launched into a sales pitch for a new credit card offer. The offer was clearly outrageous - 5% cash back on all purchases forever - so naturally I questioned her about the "all" and "forever" claims. She went back and forth with me, assuring me over and over that it was indeed all purchase categories and no time limit. It was very specific, too, for example I'd say "Are you telling me that if I spend $100 on Amazon.com I will receive $5 back?", and she'd say yes, and then I'd say "And you are telling me it doesn't expire after 6 months or something?", and she'd say no. This went on for about 15 minutes, during which I repeatedly stated that I simply do not believe the offer and need to see it in writing before I consent to anything and begged her to move on because I didn't want to miss my flight. Only after I threatened to leave, my banker agreed to move on, confirming (per my request) that she would not open the card but would instead have the credit card company send me a detailed offer letter. She then appeared to take care of my other transactions as there was a lot of typing and comments about screens taking a while to load. A week later I came back from my trip to find the new credit card in my mail - along with a standard CC disclosure which predictably spelled out cash back terms nowhere near what my banker had claimed - and to add insult to injury, not a single one of my other transactions were actually done, including one that resulted in me not having access to my money during the trip. (If it weren't for my husband's cards, I would have been in real trouble). Needless to say I was quite upset by it all, so I drove to the bank to complain in person. I spoke to the assistant manager who performed the expected customer service dance act. Per my request, he promised a follow up via a phone call or a letter where someone would tell me what specific measures they took to discipline the banker and/or to prevent this from happening in the future. I've never heard from them again. (Quick research suggests that bank employees are commonly required to sign up a certain number of people to hit their performance targets, so there is clearly a conflict of interest as far as my complaint is concerned, after all, the bank is not going to punish an employee for doing as they are told). My question is, what meaningful action can I take? In my opinion, this banker is not someone who should have access to other people's money, and I am not happy about Wells Fargo's laissez-faire attitude towards what I perceive to be outright fraud. If a regular person did this to me I could file a police report, but if it's my banker, it's just a customer service issue? Tell me it ain't so.

If your Payment Method or payment of fees is subject to other terms and conditions, as set forth in order forms, invoices or otherwise, then those other terms and conditions apply in addition to this TOS. title: Which mutual funds is Dave Ramsey talking about in The Total Money Makeover?
text: In the 2007 edition of Dave Ramsey's book The Total Money Makeover: A Proven Plan for Financial Fitness (ISBN 978-0-7852-8908-1), on pages xv & xvi, he states the following: Many intelligent but ignorant people seem to think that making a 12 percent rate of return on your money in a long-term investment is impossible. He goes on to provide some evidence from his own portfolio: I purchased a Growth and Income Stock Mutual Fund many years ago, that I still invest in, and it has average 12.78 percent per year since 1934 (72 years as of this writing). I bought another last week that has averaged over 15.43 percent per year since 1959, as of this writing. And yet another with average annual returns of 13.55 percent since 1984, and another averaging 13.51 percent since 1973, and yet another averaging 12.67 percent since 1952. Any decent broker with the heart of a teacher can, in his or her sleep, lead you to funds with long track records averaging over 12 percent. 1934 + 72 = 2006, so presumably he came up with those numbers at some point during 2006. He never identifies the specific mutual funds--not here, nor anywhere else that I've been able to find. When asked, he refers you to an "Endorsed Local Provider," i.e., to someone who pays Mr. Ramsey for leads. Given specific numbers, and a specific date range (15.43% per year from 1959 to 2006) it should be possible to determine the exact mutual funds that Mr. Ramsey is referring to. This question is two-fold: What mutual funds fit Mr. Ramsey's description? What tool did you use to determine this? One of the challenges I have found is that all the free, online mutual fund performance & rating tools I've reviewed don't look back more than 10 or perhaps 20 years. Additionally, there numbers are always use "today" or "this year" as an endpoint--you can't arbitrarily pick your endpoint. Note that this answer suggests that perhaps the first fund (12.78% per year) is The Investment Company of America® (growth-and-income fund) (symbol AIVSX for Class A, or front-loaded, shares, which is what Mr. Ramsey recommends ). The numbers don't quite align, but the question uses numbers Mr. Ramsey provided during 2012, so you would expect them to be slightly different.

title: Establishing a productivity measurement for an outbound-only Call Center?
text: I am currently trying to establish how to hold a team of outbound-only reps accountable for production each day. I don't want to set an arbitrary number, but I do find it increasingly difficult to get an accurate production number. It first started off as: Calls Made/Calls Scheduled = Production % 120 Calls Made/140 calls Scheduled = 85% Production Then I realized this isn't a fair assessment, as it isn't taking into account other factors, such as: Handling Emails from customers After Call Work Scheduled meetings and other offline time Breaks Working with other departments offline (i.e. getting help from out IT or design group) They may not need to call every person I assigned them, like if a business is listed twice with the same phone number. System downtime Calls they didn't have to make (but were scheduled to make) So then the problem turned into this trainwreck, that I needed to calculate each week, for each person. Production Hours / Scheduled hours - (email hours + ACW - meetings and offline hours + system issue hours + a guesstimate of the time they spent working with other departments + calls they didn't have to make) This is nearly impossible to calculate as most of the info isn't fully tracked (we're a small, small business) and if it is tracked, it's across multiple systems. My questions: Do you see an easier way? Do you have any experience? Is there any software that does this or connects to a third-party CRM? Can you help me keep my sanity?

title: How do I respond to constant small criticism from a supervisor?
text: I work part-time at an ice cream shop with overall a great team. However, one of my supervisors seems to always be giving me small reminders or criticism when I do a task. It almost seems like they want to snub me on every little thing. For example, small things like this: I was told to replace garbage bags an hour prior to closing, and I followed through. However, I thought it was too early because we were still receiving customers and it would give us a bad impression, but I decided to continue doing it because they had asked me to. So five minutes later, they tell me that it doesn't look good because there are still customers but I was literally instructed to do the task from them. Or when I wipe down counters, I'll forget to wipe a tiny spot and they call me out in front of other employees. Or I get reminded on tasks that are not part of my duty but another person's. I understand that I could overlook some things and will gladly accept any reminders but they are constantly reminding me every hour or so on different small things. They could simply be trying to help me out and remind me for the future, but other supervisors never have that much to say to me. Additionally, when I apologize they'll tell me that it's not something I need to apologize for and make me feel almost guilty for saying sorry. I know that I perform quite well because during performance review meetings I score quite high so I don't understand why that supervisor is so nitpicky. I have four other supervisors who are never on my case like that, just this one specifically. I'm not sure if I should speak up or if I should just tolerate it and assume that she is saying things to help me improve my performance. I just feel stressed whenever I see that I'm scheduled to work with them and brace myself for the constant small criticism.

title: Interview Qs (eg 'dealing with difficult people', 'X happens - how to respond?') when many of my experiences are from an extreme environment
text: I have around 15 years working experience already so I'm not a workplace newbie, but I've never actually "prepared" for an interview or role-played answers or anything like that (I just turn up and talk!). I've had my share of success and failure with that 'technique' - as you can imagine - so I am working on proper interview technique in the hope of improving. I am also looking to move on to a more senior level role (in a different company) due to 2 reasons - I'm now "stagnating" here, and I'm not sure about the long term viability of the job (layoffs etc) due to signals I'm picking up. I am curious about how to handle interview questions like: (I made these up based on examples on websites so there may be a better way that a real interviewer would word them...) "Can you describe a situation where you had to deal with a difficult person in another team?" "Deliverable X has to go to the customer tomorrow, but it will still take 3 days based on your estimates -- what do you do?" "What's a time you exhibited leadership?" My problem is that out of those 15 years experience, my most recent (and largest amount of time / most senior / most relevant - edited to add: 8 years here) workplace is sort of "extreme" in that I can think of examples of those situations/scenarios but have been 'conditioned' into responses that I don't think are typical or are what interviewers are looking for. For example... In the 1st question (difficult people in other teams) we have a very "conflict averse" culture on the whole (which isn't the way I am naturally) and any 'difficult behaviour' with people in other teams is handled - if you can call it that - by passive aggressive behaviour and/or escalating it to their manager... Due to this I've mostly been on the "receiving" end (manager speaking to me because of my perceived being difficult towards others) rather than handling it. I am quite comfortable with conflict myself and don't really see "difficult people" other than I have to figure out this person's motivations and then make it work for them as well as for me. Maybe I'm lucky but I don't have too many "difficulties" with people as a result! With the 2nd question about the customer wanting Deliverable X tomorrow but it will take 3 days -- the response in my workplace is to somehow find a way to make it work, even if that takes an all-nighter or two, you have to call in favours "off the record" from people in other teams, cut corners in an undetectable way (that still produces the results). I know that isn't the "right" answer to that interview question and was struggling to think what was the right answer! I asked a friend (not at this company) who said a normal response would be more like -- "figure out what we can complete by tomorrow and if we can agree with the client/product owner/sales person to deliver that "minimum" product, explain what the problem is and commit to follow up later with the "full" product in 3 days time." Thinking about "exhibiting leadership" I have a limited amount of that in my normal role, but was faced with a situation last year where due to a combination of circumstances my manager, and her manager (so the 2 levels of management above me) were unexpectedly out of the workplace for a sustained period and I had to pick up a lot of responsibilities that weren't really my place. I didn't have anyone to ask (I was the 'senior' in the team but not their manager) and had to make it up as I went along. I didn't have a 'strategy' or anything like that, I was really just surviving day to day. 'Difficult/demanding customers' - my experiences with customers mostly seem mundane compared to the time I was 16 and the shop I worked in at the time was "held up" by an armed robber and I had to defuse that situation myself! I don't think an interviewer wants to hear about that though. Question: How should I respond to interview questions similar to the above, when I don't have 'sane' recent experiences to draw on? I have come across the situations, but my examples relate to more extreme experiences. I also want to get across that I'm more than capable of dealing with (what I perceive as) "mundane" situations compared to experiences I have already. NB: I looked at this question ('Spinning' a dysfunctional workplace) from the suggested duplicates but I don't think it's a duplicate because I'm asking how to come up with sensible answers to questions like "dealing with difficult people", rather than presenting the "dysfunctional" experiences in a positive light. Added a country tag but I don't think this is country specific.

title: First software job is miserable. First, are my concerns valid? Second, if they are, what do I do?
text: I'm in my first job as a software engineering grad in Canada. I took a job with a government agency this September after an offer fell through late (April) and I took the first job I could (as you will see, I am a person who needs proof that I am capable and that offer was a beacon in a mess). It has good pay (especially for my area which is not a software hub), but I can't wait to get out of there every day. The problems: They are extremely cheap when it comes to software spending for the developers. Bug tracking system? Too expensive. So we just don't track bugs in a centralized way. Independent QA systems? No, the three QA testers must either use one test server or learn to compile software themselves. We were told to just keep renewing our IDE trials every 30 days, so they don't pay for those either. We have very minimal access to cloud services because of the cost. We have to go easy on Jenkins to conserve hard drive space. The team is inexperienced as everyone gets hired on a temp to hire contract. The median time for a developer there is currently 6 months. The only person to be there more than a year is our lead. As a result, nobody knows anything about the systems. They oppose documentation because of "Agile." Forget documenting code, they don't even document features. I have been repeatedly assigned to develop features which already exist. Things just move so slowly. Each developer is supposed to do 21 points of work a sprint and a sprint is two weeks. I have consistently finished in under 6 days, including unit and Selenium tests (myself and the new QA are the only ones to do this type of testing). They don't finish and accuse me of "pushing the pace." My background. I have never had a proper software job before, so I don't know if it the environment or the job I hate. Past jobs were in quantitative finance, where the work was highly individual, as well as at a startup, where I was one of two developers. This is the first job where I don't make my own calls as to the pace of work or how complex things are, or don't get much insight into the project and just get handed widgets to do. What are my options after 6 months? A friend offered me a spot with her startup (I have done all their prior dev work), but with a recession plausible in the near future in Canada, I'm worried that 6 months as a government worker and time as the main dev at a startup will look absurd on a resume. I realize this isn't a discussion forum, so I have two clear questions. Is this normal for software development? Is it representative of your experiences? If it is not, then what can I do for my market value in the next few months (I'll stick around until at least March to avoid seeming like a job hopper).to exit effectively? I have a good engineering degree from a top Canadian university, good grades, a pile of hackathon awards (and can get more if they are useful), have a decent project to show off (my friend's tech startup website), etc. I have an ok StackOverflow profile too if that is worth anything (2000-3000 points and 150ish answers). It's just how to deal with landing badly after university which scares me.
